text1: The reactor technology that spawned spinally-mounted long-cycle ship weapons also ushered in an age of short-pulse energy weapons. Short-cycle lance batteries are an archetypal example of these. Though mid-ranged, they are accurate and quick at boring holes through hull and armor plate, and can even put some pressure on energy shielding.

The Caspian Sea-class frigate has been continually upgraded over it's centuries of service, been one of the few designs in service through the Second Committee to the current day. 
Like all GMS products, the Caspian Sea is reliable and easy to service, a dependable lineship that is  capable in both fleet combat and smaller-scale engagements. It is equipped with an advanced sensor suite that allows it to pick out a target for the rest of the fleet, providing precision locks on key structural strongpoints.

Short-spool superheavy mounts are a fairly recent innovation in the long history of spatial warfare, trading the decisive impacts of traditonal superheavy weapons for consistent firepower that remains a class above that of a ship's main battery.

Large cannon arrays are the most common manifestation of that philosophy, with this particular pattern firing all nine guns at once.

Once a lifeless world, Sioa is now dotted with mining infrastructure and ringed by industry, with the fleet's mobile shipyards wasting no time in creating a permanent Schedule 4 fabrication facility in orbit.
Nearly half of RINGAD Koenig emerged from this gate rather than their destination blinkgate.

Formed from the reborn polities of a devastated Earth, and now over five thousand years old, Union is a (mostly) post-scarcity society and the undisputed hegemon of the Orion Arm. The recent start of the Second Distal War against it's only real rival, led to the dispatch of a full sixth of it's naval strength in the form of two Ring Fleets. However, nearly half of the Tenth Ring Fleet (RINGAD Koenig), along with it's commander, would be lost in an unprecedented blinkspace rupture as they made their final gate transit before the long voyage to Boundary Garden.

This dissappeared force emerged in the Persean Sector through a long-dormant gate in a system far from the core. Upon ascertaining that there was no easy way back home, the fleet fell back on seldom-used isolation contingencies. The existing soldier's councils and scattered civilian elements in the fleet were hastily organized and reconfigured into a proper governing body. Though there were several hiccups, the newly (re)formed Union had plenty of time. Much of the fleet's mobile fabrication facilities had been dragged with them into the Persean Sector, and the ample supply stocks which had once been intended to fuel an expeditionary war allowed them to wait while the government sorted itself out and the Printers got to work on the planet below.

Now well estabished, this new Union turns its eye towards the Core Worlds, drawn by garbled fragments of transmissions and the corrupted databanks of discovered derelicts.
A temporary redirection of computing power and sensor arrays towards a particular enemy vessel allows for the creation and broadcast of optimised firing solutions throughout the fleet.
